summary: Chronic airway inflammation causing episodic wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from variable, reversible airflow obstruction; affects adolescents and adults, often with an atopic/allergic component. Managed with stepped inhaled therapy (controller +/- reliever) escalated to symptom control and exacerbation risk, with biologic add-on at the top step for refractory disease. Reliever strategy - the guidelines disagree: GINA 2025's preferred Track 1 uses as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol as both maintenance and reliever (MART) across Steps 1-5 for ages 12+, and no longer prefers SABA-alone as reliever at any step. US NAEPP 2020 - still the current federal guideline, no newer edition exists as of Oct 2026 - permits daily ICS plus as-needed SABA as an equal Step 2 option, and only recommends ICS-formoterol-as-reliever (SMART) from Step 3 (moderate-to-severe persistent, ages 4+) upward, not down to mild disease the way GINA does. NAEPP also warns ICS-formoterol must never be used as a reliever by patients on ICS-salmeterol maintenance. Biologic eligibility converges at Step 5 (failure of high-dose ICS-LABA); phenotype, not line of therapy, differentiates among agents.

news.what: GINA 2025 report received a minor correction (pediatric nebulized salbutamol dose only; the Track 1 MART strategy is unchanged from the May 2025 report).
Airsupra (albuterol-budesonide) label expanded with BATURA trial data on exacerbation-risk reduction in mild asthma. Company-sourced; Tier 3, not independently confirmed against an FDA label action.

FDA approved Omlyclo (omalizumab-igec), the first omalizumab biosimilar and the first respiratory biosimilar approved in the US, with an interchangeability designation; carries the same anaphylaxis boxed warning as reference Xolair.
